output.answer:
I can't tell the cause from your message alone. The docs I read describe several separate things that can stop traces appearing, and which one applies depends on your SDK and integration. These are the checks I found.

**1. Check that tracing isn't disabled**
- `WEAVE_DISABLED=true` turns tracing off for the entire program. It is read only once, when functions are defined [S6].
- In Python, `weave.init(..., settings={"disabled": True})` disables tracing for that client [S2].
- Code run inside `with tracing_disabled():` isn't traced [S3].

**2. Flush before a short script exits (Python agent-turn example)**
One docs example logs an agent turn with `log_turn`. It notes that `weave.init` exports spans from a background thread, and it calls `trace.get_tracer_provider().force_flush(30_000)` before a short script exits [S7]. That example is about agent turns. I didn't find a page that says the same applies to every kind of trace.

**3. TypeScript SDK**
- Weave automatically patches supported libraries such as OpenAI when it loads. Edge cases can interfere, such as ESM-only projects, bundlers like Next.js, and constrained runtimes. The docs say to start with "Advanced usage and troubleshooting" if you see missing traces [S1].
- For ESM projects where you can't pass CLI flags, the docs suggest `export NODE_OPTIONS="--import=weave/instrument"`. They warn that this affects all Node.js processes in the environment [S4].

**4. OpenTelemetry-based integrations (example: Koog)**
- Verify that `WEAVE_API_KEY`, `WEAVE_ENTITY`, and `WEAVE_PROJECT_NAME` are set correctly [S5].
- Confirm your environment can reach `https://trace.wandb.ai`, and that the exporter is configured as in the guide's examples [S5].

**To narrow it down**, tell me:
- Whether you use Python or TypeScript.
- Which library or integration you're tracing.
- Whether the script exits quickly.
- Any errors you see.

sources.heading: Environment variable
sources.text:
## Environment variable

Use an environment variable when you want to disable tracing for the entire program without modifying application code.

To unconditionally disable tracing for the entire program, set the environment variable `WEAVE_DISABLED=true`.

`WEAVE_DISABLED` is read only once, at function-definition time. You can't use this variable to toggle tracing at runtime.

## Context manager

To conditionally disable tracing only within a specific block of code, use a tracing context manager. Use `with tracing_disabled()` to suppress tracing **only for the function calls executed inside the `with` block**. Use it in application code to scope which calls shouldn't be logged.

**Python**

```python lines theme={"system"}
import weave
from weave.trace.context.call_context import tracing_disabled

client = weave.init('your-team/your-project-name')

@weave.op
def my_op():
    ...

with tracing_disabled():
    my_op()
```

**TypeScript**

```plaintext theme={"system"}
This feature is not available for the TypeScript SDK yet.
```

Although tracing behavior is fixed when functions are defined, you can use this for runtime control when you combine it with application logic. For example, wrap the context manager in a conditional to dynamically enable or disable tracing based on a runtime value:

**Python**

```python lines theme={"system"}
if should_trace:
    my_op()
else:
    with tracing_disabled():
        my_op()
```

**TypeScript**

```plaintext theme={"system"}
This feature is not available for the TypeScript SDK yet.
```

sources.heading: Test the signal
sources.text:
## Test the signal

Before you test, deploy the endpoint at an HTTPS URL that's on the allowed hosts, and register it.

Log one completed turn, then check the **Signals** tab. Scoring is asynchronous, so the result appears after a delay.

```python lines theme={"system"}
import uuid

from opentelemetry import trace

import weave
from weave.conversation import Message, log_turn

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

result = log_turn(
    conversation_id=f"sample-{uuid.uuid4().hex}",
    agent_name="sample-support-agent",
    system_instructions=["Answer the user accurately and concisely."],
    messages=[Message.user("What are your support hours?")],
    output_messages=[
        Message.assistant(
            "Our support team is available Monday through Friday, 9am to 5pm Eastern."
        )
    ],
)

# weave.init exports spans from a background thread. Flush before a short script exits.
trace.get_tracer_provider().force_flush(30_000)
print(result.conversation_id, result.trace_ids)
```

Your endpoint receives a V2 request with `scoring_target.type` set to `agent_turn`, and Weave records the result as feedback on that turn.

# Score agent turns with a remote scorer

> Score Weave agent turns with your own HTTP endpoint and see the results as tags or ratings on the Signals tab.

A remote scorer signal scores each completed agent turn with an HTTP endpoint that you host, instead of with an LLM judge. When a turn ends, the Weave agent scoring worker sends the turn to your endpoint in an HTTP `POST` and records the response as feedback on the turn. The result appears as a tag or rating on the **Signals** tab of the [Agents view](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-signals.md).

This page covers remote scorers for agent turns. To score Calls traced with `@weave.op`, see [Score Calls with remote scorers](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/remote-scorers.md). You configure remote scorers with the Python SDK or the Weave UI. The TypeScript SDK doesn't include `RemoteScorer`.

## Context manager

To conditionally disable tracing only within a specific block of code, use a tracing context manager. Use `with tracing_disabled()` to suppress tracing **only for the function calls executed inside the `with` block**. Use it in application code to scope which calls shouldn't be logged.

**Python**

```python lines theme={"system"}
import weave
from weave.trace.context.call_context import tracing_disabled

client = weave.init('your-team/your-project-name')

@weave.op
def my_op():
    ...

with tracing_disabled():
    my_op()
```

**TypeScript**

```plaintext theme={"system"}
This feature is not available for the TypeScript SDK yet.
```

Although tracing behavior is fixed when functions are defined, you can use this for runtime control when you combine it with application logic. For example, wrap the context manager in a conditional to dynamically enable or disable tracing based on a runtime value:

**Python**

```python lines theme={"system"}
if should_trace:
    my_op()
else:
    with tracing_disabled():
        my_op()
```

**TypeScript**

```plaintext theme={"system"}
This feature is not available for the TypeScript SDK yet.
```

all_read_evidence.heading: Test the signal
all_read_evidence.text:
## Test the signal

Before you test, deploy the endpoint at an HTTPS URL that's on the allowed hosts, and register it.

Log one completed turn, then check the **Signals** tab. Scoring is asynchronous, so the result appears after a delay.

```python lines theme={"system"}
import uuid

from opentelemetry import trace

import weave
from weave.conversation import Message, log_turn

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

result = log_turn(
    conversation_id=f"sample-{uuid.uuid4().hex}",
    agent_name="sample-support-agent",
    system_instructions=["Answer the user accurately and concisely."],
    messages=[Message.user("What are your support hours?")],
    output_messages=[
        Message.assistant(
            "Our support team is available Monday through Friday, 9am to 5pm Eastern."
        )
    ],
)

# weave.init exports spans from a background thread. Flush before a short script exits.
trace.get_tracer_provider().force_flush(30_000)
print(result.conversation_id, result.trace_ids)
```

Your endpoint receives a V2 request with `scoring_target.type` set to `agent_turn`, and Weave records the result as feedback on that turn.

# Score agent turns with a remote scorer

> Score Weave agent turns with your own HTTP endpoint and see the results as tags or ratings on the Signals tab.

A remote scorer signal scores each completed agent turn with an HTTP endpoint that you host, instead of with an LLM judge. When a turn ends, the Weave agent scoring worker sends the turn to your endpoint in an HTTP `POST` and records the response as feedback on the turn. The result appears as a tag or rating on the **Signals** tab of the [Agents view](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-signals.md).

This page covers remote scorers for agent turns. To score Calls traced with `@weave.op`, see [Score Calls with remote scorers](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/remote-scorers.md). You configure remote scorers with the Python SDK or the Weave UI. The TypeScript SDK doesn't include `RemoteScorer`.

## View a linked run in the Traces table

When you call a function decorated with `@weave.op` inside a `wandb.init()` context of your ML pipeline, Weave automatically associates the trace with the active [Weights & Biases run](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/runs.md). The **Traces** table in the Weave UI links each trace to its associated runs.

To view the runs linked to your traces:

1. Run a script that calls traced functions inside a `wandb.init()` context, such as the training example in [Use Weave panels](#use-weave-panels).
2. Open the [Weights & Biases UI](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and select your project.
3. In the **Weave** project sidebar, click **Traces**. The **Traces** table displays links to any associated runs.
4. Open a trace from the **Traces** table to inspect the linked run and review its experiment context.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The Weave TypeScript SDK doesn't support linking traces to Weights & Biases runs.

# Score agent turns with a remote scorer

> Score Weave agent turns with your own HTTP endpoint and see the results as tags or ratings on the Signals tab.

A remote scorer signal scores each completed agent turn with an HTTP endpoint that you host, instead of with an LLM judge.
